title: The Evening Brief: Bitcoin slides, but whale buyers move in; ETF outflows persist
author: Crypto Cronkite
bottom_line: Thursday brought broad crypto weakness, bitcoin down 1.6%, the market down 4.9% by cap, yet whale flows contradict the selloff: $119.5 million in bitcoin moved onto exchanges in 24 hours, continuing a fourth straight week of accumulation to major institutional custodians. The desk's boards show funding rates favoring shorts in ethereum and solana despite predominantly long positioning, a setup that may test the tape as leverage unwinds. Watch for whether whale buying sustains through coming days and whether ETF flows reverse.
body: Thursday's tape split between price and flow. The broader market contracted 4.9% by total market cap to $2.78 trillion, per the desk's boards. Over the longer window, however, bitcoin remains up 5.3% on the month and ethereum up 3.4%, though both assets are well below their 12-month highs: bitcoin trades 34.4% below its $124,739 peak and ethereum 47.2% below $4,690.84.

The desk's Whale Watch board presents a counterpoint to the day's selloff. A net $119.5 million in bitcoin moved onto exchanges in the 24-hour window, the fourth consecutive week of such flows: the weeks ending September 17, September 24, October 1, and October 8 each saw $324 million, $1,091 million, $704 million, and $572 million move onto exchanges respectively. The largest single moves into Coinbase Institutional totaled $170.8 million, $137.0 million, and $100.1 million, suggesting institutional buyers are absorbing supply. Against this, Kraken saw $80.8 million in bitcoin move off exchange, the largest outflow segment.

Spot ETF flows, by contrast, turned sharply negative. Bitcoin ETFs saw outflows of $25.9 million on Thursday and $291.9 million over the past five sessions, per the desk's board. Ethereum ETF outflows were steeper: $4.8 million on the day and $455.8 million over five sessions, marking eight consecutive days of outflows.

Leverage positioning shows shorts accumulating in several assets. On OKX, bitcoin's long-short ratio stands at 1.69, ethereum at 2.39, and solana at 2.36, all well-weighted toward longs. Funding rates tell a different story: bitcoin's 8-hour rate sits at a modest 0.0033%, while ethereum trades at negative 0.0054% and solana at negative 0.007%, indicating short-side pressure. Over the past few hours, shorts liquidated $1.16 million in bitcoin on OKX and $848.8 thousand in ethereum, though longs saw smaller losses.
Fear and Greed index sits at 64 (Greed), within its 30-day range of 50 to 78. Stablecoin reserves stand at $312.3 billion, up 1.1% over the past month, suggesting dry powder remains on sidelines.
